title: The slope of a cubic from its secants
statement: For $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x + 1$, find the slope of the secant from $x = 2$ over the runs $h = 1$, $0.1$ and $0.01$, then the slope they close on, $f'(2)$, and the tangent line at $x = 2$.

artefact.caption: Each run: the secant's slope $\frac{f(2 + h) - f(2)}{h}$

steps.title: Read the problem
steps.note: A secant from $x = 2$ over a run $h$ rises $f(2 + h) - f(2)$, so its slope is $\frac{f(2 + h) - f(2)}{h}$. As $h$ shrinks, the secant turns onto the tangent, and its slope onto $f'(2)$.

steps.title: Run $h = 0.1$
steps.note: $f(2.1) = 9.261 - 13.23 + 4.2 + 1 = 1.231$, so the slope is $\frac{0.231}{0.1} = 2.31$: much closer to the tangent's.

steps.title: The slope they close on
steps.note: The slopes $6$, $2.31$, $2.0301$ close on $f'(2) = 3(2)^2 - 6(2) + 2 = 2$, from the power rule $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x + 2$. The tangent through $(2, 1)$ is $y = 1 + 2(x - 2) = 2x - 3$.
